$comment: CURRENT STATE, not history. The keys here must equal the set of OPEN PRs
exactly — control-plane:verify FAILS on a missing entry AND on a stale one.
Why both directions. An unclassified open PR is background state: #1623 sat
open for weeks while main carried a stale route count, and nobody was wrong,
because nobody owned it. A leftover row is the mirror image — this file
carried ACTIVE rows for #1623, #1638, #1679 and #1680 after they closed or
merged, so a current-state registry was asserting things that had stopped
being true. Git holds the history; this holds the present.
ONE EXCEPTION, and it is exact. A row whose PR has MERGED and whose
merge_commit_sha equals the verified checkout’s HEAD is TRANSITIONALLY
CLOSED rather than stale. Without it, a PR that carries its own row makes
main fail this check the second it merges, and the only exits are another PR
(same problem, recursively) or a direct push — which is what actually
happened on 2026-08-30, twice, bypassing branch protection. A control whose
only escape is bypassing another control is a defect in the first one.
It is merge IDENTITY, not "merged recently" or "within N commits": the moment
any other commit lands, HEAD moves and the row fails again. It survives its
own merge and nothing more. Clear it in the next ordinary PR, which adds its
own row at the same time.
AND ITS MIRROR, before the merge. A row that lives in its own PR is absent
from main for that PR’s whole flight, so the missing-row rule would fail main
from the moment such a PR opens. A row absent here but PRESENT in this file at
that PR’s own head is IN FLIGHT, not unclassified. Absent at the head, or
unreadable there, still fails — #1623 sat open for weeks with no row anywhere
and must stay caught. Arriving has to be proven, never assumed.
disposition — what the PR IS:
ACTIVE, HUMAN_TEST_PENDING, STALE, SUPERSEDED, AUTOMATION_RESIDUE, UNKNOWN
worktree_policy — what may HAPPEN to its checkout:
KEEP                    never park it automatically
PARK_IF_REPRODUCIBLE    park it once clean and pushed; the branch stays
worktree_policy IS NOW THE SECOND OF TWO GATES, and is on its way out. Since
2026-08-30 a checkout is released by its own .helm/workspace.json
(parkPolicy), which covers the window before a PR exists — the window this
field cannot see. Both gates must permit, so this field can only ever make the
answer more conservative.
It is kept for now rather than deleted in the same change, for one concrete
reason: #1659 is PARKED. There is no checkout on disk to carry a marker, so
deleting this field would delete the only recorded authorization for it.
Remove the field when #1659 is resolved, or when its worktree is recreated and
its intent written into the marker — and remove the residue check’s policy
validation in the same change.
The second field exists because the first was being asked to imply it. On
2026-08-30 `--retire` parked a concurrent session's worktree (#1681) purely
because the checkout was clean, pushed, and no process was visible to lsof
at that instant. Negative process detection is not proof of inactivity. For
an OPEN PR, dispensability now has to be stated, not inferred.
ACTIVE and UNKNOWN always KEEP, whatever this field says — a mis-typed
policy beside them fails safe.
